title: Golden prompts harness and deployment safeguards for cost-opt autosuggests
creator: Ethan Ramirez
description: Build an automated evaluation harness that runs a curated set of golden prompts and structured tests whenever batching/caching or other cost-saving inference configs are proposed. The harness will produce a compact regression signal used by the cost optimizer's safe-apply flow so we can auto-apply low-risk config changes while preventing quality regressions. This ticket covers the eval suite design, metric selection, threshold policy, integration with the config apply pipeline, UI hooks for approvals, and the automated rollback triggers used during canary and global rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible golden prompt suite (initially ~400 prompts spanning extraction/summarization/conversational templates) stored in s3 and accessible by CI
A composite regression score computed per candidate config combining semantic-similarity, token-likelihood delta, and task-specific exact-match where applicable
Defined acceptance thresholds per task category documented and enforced by the safe-apply pipeline
Safe-apply flow updated to require passed evals before auto-apply; if canary fails, automatic rollback triggers and alerting fire
End-to-end integration tests and a console view that shows pass/fail, key diffs, and links to failing examples

decisions: Golden prompts will be split into three task buckets: extraction (high exact-match weight), summarization (semantic similarity weight), and dialog (coherence & hallucination heuristics)
Composite score = 0.5 * normalized semantic-similarity + 0.3 * likelihood-delta-normalized + 0.2 * task-exact-match (weights tunable via config)
Primary semantic similarity metric: embedding cosine similarity using production embed model; fallback for short texts: token-level overlap + normalized edit distance

Acceptance thresholds (initial): extraction >= 0.995 pass-rate on exact-match test cases; summarization avg embedding-similarity delta >= -0.02 vs baseline; dialog top-level coherence drop <= 0.015 composite points
When candidate config meets thresholds it is eligible for auto-apply; if it fails the canary by composite drop >= 0.02 or >0.5% golden prompt failures it triggers automated rollback
We will store all eval artifacts (inputs, baseline outputs, candidate outputs, embeddings, scores) for 90 days in a cost-optimized bucket for audit and debugging

rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run in CI for every candidate config (no traffic). 2) If pass, mark as 'canary-eligible' and deploy to 1% traffic for 6 hours. 3) Monitor composite score, per-task pass rate, 95th p99 latency, and error-rate. 4) If metrics stable and regression delta < configured per-task thresholds, ramp to 10% for 12 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, then global. 5) Any trigger (composite drop >= 0.02, >0.5% new golden prompt failures, error-rate spike >0.2pp, latency increase >10% p95) initiates immediate automated rollback and an incident page is created
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring components, integration test that runs full golden suite comparing baseline and candidate, simulated canary test using traffic replay for latency/throughput, and chaos test that deliberately injects a regressing config to validate rollback automation. Manual QA: PM-led review of failing examples and UX signoff on console card.
notes: Trade-offs: smaller prompt suite runs faster and reduces CI cost but risks missing edge-case regressions; larger suite increases confidence but slows release cadence. We will start with a balanced 400-prompt set and iterate. Long-term: use sampled live-user transcripts to augment static golden prompts for low-frequency regressions. Ensure auditors can reconstruct failures using stored artifacts.
